Definition: from G303 and G2875; to beat back, i.e. check:--hinder.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: 'Ye did run well; who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth?' Paul asks the Galatians who cut in on them and broke their stride — they were running the race well, and someone stepped across their path and stopped them. It is the word for a runner tripped up mid-course.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for hindering carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the race — the Galatians were running well, and someone cut in and broke their stride.
